edits.before: A quadrotor is a benign case for simulation. Its dynamics are differentially flat in position and heading, even with linear rotor drag <Cite id="faessler-flatness-2018" />, and standard models cover its dynamics, estimation and control <Cite id="mahony-multirotor-2012" />. Flight also has no contact: an aerial robot either flies in free space or has already failed. Racing quadrotors still exceed 100 km/h and accelerate at several times gravity <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />.
edits.after:
A quadrotor is a benign case for simulation. edits.before: The admissible forces form the <Term id="friction-cone">friction cone</Term> around the inward normal, with half-angle $\alpha = \arctan \mu$. In the plane the cone is a wedge; in space it is a quadratic cone, and approximating it by a polyhedral one keeps the analysis linear <Cite id="murray-li-sastry-1994" /> <Cite id="prattichizzo-trinkle-2016" />. A soft-finger contact adds a torsional moment about the normal, bounded by a torsional coefficient times the normal load <Cite id="murray-li-sastry-1994" />.

edits.before: Moravec and Elfes projected wide-angle sonar readings from different sensors and robot positions onto a 2D <Term id="occupancy-grid">occupancy grid</Term>. Each reading marked a probably empty beam interior and an uncertain reflecting point near the measured range, and overlapping readings refined these constraints. Zero represented unknown occupancy, and negative and positive values probably empty and probably occupied cells <Cite id="moravec-elfes-1985" />. OctoMap carries the three states into 3D in a compressed octree <Cite id="octomap-2013" />.
edits.after:
Moravec and Elfes projected wide-angle sonar readings from different sensors and robot positions onto a 2D <Term id="occupancy-grid">occupancy grid</Term>. Each reading marked a probably empty beam interior and an uncertain reflecting point near the measured range, and overlapping readings refined these constraints. Zero represented unknown occupancy, and negative and positive values probably empty and probably occupied cells <Cite id="moravec-elfes-1985" />. OctoMap carries the three states into 3D in a compressed octree <Cite id="octomap-2013" />. Step through the figure below to see one mug stored four ways.

edits.before: The SO-101 is a 3D-printed arm with six <Term id="degrees-of-freedom">degrees of freedom</Term>, five joints plus a gripper, built from STS3215 servos. Its community BOM for one follower arm totals \$121.94 in the US column <Cite id="so-arm100-repo-2026" />. Seeed Studio sells the SO-ARM101 Pro at \$295 unassembled or \$299 assembled, with 12-bit magnetic encoders and a 500 g payload <Cite id="seeed-so-arm101-pro-2026" />. LeRobot runs ACT, π0 and SmolVLA policies on these arms <Cite id="lerobot-docs-2026" />.

edits.before: In ALOHA, an operator drives a leader arm that twins the follower, so demonstrations arrive in the robot's joint space. ACT, the [action-chunking](/manipulation/action-chunking) policy built for that rig, learned six bimanual tasks, each from about 10 minutes of demonstrations. It reached 84 to 96% final success on four of them, 64% on taping and 20% on threading a velcro tie. The paper put the bimanual setup at \$18k, or \$20k with add-ons such as cameras <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />.

In the gold-medal "Use a key" event of Holson's Humanoid Olympics, a keyring with at least two keys and a keychain is dropped into the robot's waiting palm or gripper.
